_about: Lore data (docs/lore/README.md; decisions 257, 258): entries with facts, each fact saying who knows it. Code uses only status agreed. Facts, never lines to say.

entries.name: the Blood Rot's land
entries.summary: The region the Blood Rot raid, with their mine at its heart and the town at a distance from it.

facts.text: The land around the mine is dead: no crops, no beasts, nothing living.
Other regions lie beyond the Blood Rot's land.

entries.name: the Woodlands
entries.summary: The Woodlands, where Umbrage sits, with the farmsteads and fields around it, far from the mine (Jeff, 2026-10-22: "Held sit in the Woodlands"; the town renamed Umbrage, Jeff 2026-10-24).

facts.text: Umbrage sits in the Woodlands.
Farmsteads and fields lie near the town.

entries.name: the town
entries.summary: Where the players and their companions belong, and where the stockpile is.

entries.name: the old farmstead
entries.summary: An old farmstead in the wilds, abandoned, with tools and bandages left inside (Jeff, 2026-10-22; built by maps' 827 as a farm gone to ruin west of the crossroads, its cache bandaging kits, a knife and a pick); not the Blood Rot's doing.

facts.text: The old farmstead in the wilds stands abandoned; tools and bandages lie inside.

entries.name: the pond
entries.summary: The wilds' fishing pond, far west of Umbrage by the west road (maps' reed_pond at (33,120), "the pond", holder nobody), with the other waters that fish: two pools (110..116 x 57..60 west of the north road; 221..223 x 224..228 east of the woodlot post) and the river's wide reach (60..77 x 16..40) in the far north-west (805 amended (8); environment's fish rise). No name of its own until Jeff picks one (Reed Pond is asked). Package "wilds basics: pond".

facts.text: Far west of town there is a pond: take the road out to the crossroads and keep on west along the west road almost to its end, and the pond lies beside it.
Reeds grow along the pond's edge.
Fish rise in the pond, and it is nobody's: anyone may fish it.
Fish feed keenest at dawn and at dusk, and more in a soft rain, rising more often and biting sooner then; at night they hardly feed.
There are two pools with fish in them too: a small one south-east of town, just east of the woodlot post, and a bigger one west of the north road, a good way north of the crossroads.
In the far north-west of the wilds, west of where the north road ends, the river runs wide and deep, and there are fish in that reach.

entries.name: Towerside
entries.summary: The land south of Umbrage round the Old Tower and its river, the map levels/held (Jeff picked the name, 2026-11-04, from lore's set worded by voice; maps' 651 amended).

facts.text: Towerside is the land south of Umbrage, round the Old Tower.

entries.name: the Old Tower
entries.summary: The Old Tower across the river from Umbrage: a broken-down castle the ancients lived in, conquered in the battle; its fallen warriors were buried before the people moved on, and nothing is known of them since. Snagfin keeps his counter there (Jeff, 2026-10-22).

facts.text: The Old Tower, across the river from Umbrage, is a broken-down castle the ancients lived in.
The Old Tower, the ancients' castle, was conquered in the battle, and its fallen warriors were buried before the people moved on.
Nothing is known of the ancients' history, or of them since they left.
No dead lie by the Old Tower: the dead are in the barrows, and the tower is where they lived.
Snagfin the goblin keeps his counter in the Old Tower.

entries.name: the temple
entries.summary: The town's temple, kept by a priest, where the fallen are brought back.

facts.text: The town has a temple, and a priest keeps it.
A charm blessed at the temple becomes Theus's.
Whoever the temple brings back makes a gold offering there, and is brought back even with less gold than it asks.

entries.name: the Last Light Mughouse
entries.summary: Umbrage's tavern on the west of the square, three floors (Jeff named it, 2026-11-05: "Last Light Mughouse"); locals call it the Mughouse.

facts.text: Umbrage's tavern is the Last Light Mughouse, and locals call it the Mughouse.
The Mughouse has a hearth in its common room, ale on tap at the counter, and five rooms to hire upstairs under an attic.
facts.sight: the hearth and the rooms upstairs

facts.text: The Mughouse's sign hangs by its door: a board painted with a burning lantern and no letters, with a small iron lantern at the bracket's tip.
The Last Light keeps a lamp in the window nearest its door that never goes out, day or night.

entries.name: the smithy
entries.summary: Umbrage's smithy, cold since its smith went below the castle after the great dwarven forge and was taken.

facts.text: Umbrage's smithy has stood cold since the smith went below the castle.

entries.name: the healer's hut
entries.summary: A healer's hut out in the wilds, where a medicine man lives and the fallen are brought back.

facts.text: Out in the wilds stands a healer's hut, where a medicine man lives.

entries.name: Cravenhold
entries.summary: The orc stronghold, outside the forest, in a land where the trees have been stripped (Jeff, 2026-10-27; maps' world_plane place "stronghold").

facts.text: Cravenhold is the orc stronghold, outside the forest, in a land where the trees have been stripped.

entries.name: the castle
entries.summary: An ancient, dilapidated castle built by dwarven stone smiths over a known entrance to the shifting labyrinths, to guard it; mostly overrun now (docs/lore/castle.md).

facts.text: The castle is ancient and dilapidated.
The castle was built by dwarven stone smiths, plain and utilitarian.
The dwarves built the castle over the labyrinths, as a cover over a known entrance, to guard it.
The castle guards a treasure that was rumoured and never found.
The castle is no longer dwarven; it is mostly overrun.
The maps of the labyrinths below the castle were lost long ago.
The labyrinths shift: their ways are never the same twice for long, which is why their treasures were never carried out and why adventurers still come.
Dwarven artifacts come from the dungeons below the castle.
Who has overrun the castle: the Blood Rot, their orc or kobold allies, something from below, or several at once.

entries.name: the mine
entries.summary: An old mine, the heart of the Blood Rot's land, over the fallen star.

facts.text: The old mine is the heart of the Blood Rot's land, and they live in and around it.
The deeper into the mine, the stronger the Blood Rot are.
The mine was dug toward where the star fell.

entries.name: the tower over the mine
entries.summary: A tower over the mine, built by orcs to dark elven designs, whose shifting inside still holds old artifacts and treasures.

facts.text: A tower stands over the mine.
The tower over the mine was built by orcish labour to the designs of dark elven architects, in their majestic style.
The tower over the mine holds old artifacts and treasures; dark elven artifacts come from it.
The inside of the tower over the mine shifts, perhaps by magic; its treasures have never all been carried out, and adventurers still come.

entries.name: the fallen star
entries.summary: Deep in the mine lies the source of the rot: a star that fell into the land many thousands of years ago.

facts.text: Deep in the Blood Rot's mine lies a fallen star, the source of the rot.
Common folk call it a fallen star.
Those who live near the mine call it the rot-source.
Those the Blood Rot take are carried down toward the star and are not seen again.

entries.name: Hollowfell
entries.summary: The town's old iron workings in the hills, dug by the first folk and lost when the deep seams broke into caves below; whatever is strongest in the hills holds it (Jeff, 2026-11-03: "I like the name of Hollowfell", and lore's story). Its level is 790's mine (57e3f9e2).

facts.text: Hollowfell, in the hills, was dug for iron by the town's first folk, and its ore made the town's tools and blades for generations.
Hollowfell's deep seams broke into caves no one knew of; what lived there came up, and the miners left.
Since Hollowfell was lost, whatever is strongest in the hills holds it.
When Hollowfell was lost, the town turned to the barrow's gold, and that is part of why Umbrage is cursed.

entries.name: the broken watchtower
entries.summary: A broken watchtower on the hills plateau, north of the shieling (maps' 778, hills (186,18)): the ancients of the Old Tower kept watch over the hills road from it. Draft till Jeff's wording check; the guild sheet's lean makes it the Templars' house.

facts.text: The ancients who lived in the Old Tower kept watch over the hills road from the watchtower on the plateau.
The watchtower on the plateau was broken when the Old Tower was taken.
A cold fire-basin at the top of the watchtower is where the watch lit its warning fire.

entries.name: the lone great oak
entries.summary: A lone great oak between the hills' rivers (maps' 778, hills (111,159)), older than the town. Jeff picked it for the Druids' hall, a hollow oak massive enough to walk into (2026-11-03); that stays out of the facts until the hall is built.

facts.text: The lone great oak between the rivers is older than the town, and the hill herders won't let it be felled.
A herder who loses a beast ties a strip of cloth to the great oak, and they say the beast comes home.

entries.name: the standing stone
entries.summary: A standing stone on the hills plateau's east edge (maps' 778, hills (199,70)), older than the ancients.

facts.text: The standing stone on the plateau is older than the ancients; some say the old tribe raised it for their many gods.
No one can read the worn carving on the standing stone, and nobody sleeps beside it.

entries.name: the hills road
entries.summary: The road through the hills, west to the wilds and east to the spur and the shieling, and the small stories off it (maps' 778).

facts.text: The hills road is older than the town: the ancients laid it, and the town's folk have cut new names over the milestones' worn marks.
A traveller on the hills road was caught by raiders; they took his pack but missed a note in his coat.
Before the raiders caught him, the traveller hid his goods under a cairn north of the hills road, east of where he lies.
Some years ago hill folk and Blood Rot raiders fought in the hills, and the broken gear still lies where they fell.
One of the hill folk who fell in that fight was buried where he fell, the barrow being too far, and someone still brings his grave fresh offerings.
His kin left the town for the hills after the fight and keeps a lean-to there, and is often out.
